title: The Wonder in the Dark Room
blurb: A little lit box writes back, one word at a time, and nobody ever wrote it a rulebook. A teacher opens the case (WHO TAUGHT IT?), files the machine's own makers' first-day admission, pins three suspects, glimpses a shelf of old certainties and a wall of forecasts, and rewinds to the war years and a lamp in Chicago.

shots.visual: THIS SHOT: close on the little lit box: the question drops in as type slugs, and an answer rises back, slug by slug, locked to each spoken word. The push-in continues until the screen's rectangle fills the frame and its edges become a soft glowing frame of light against the dark. Inside it, staged as a typesetter's bench rather than a user interface: the question appears first as a short line of cast type slugs dropping into a composing stick (typeSlugs, reveal 0 to 1 across L0102), a few words long, deliberately soft and slightly out of focus so we feel the act rather than read the content (illustrative tokens only, e.g. a question about why the sky is blue). Then on L0103 a second composing stick below begins to fill: one slug at a time, each sort rising out of an unseen case and dropping into place with a tiny bounce and a puff of lamplit dust, the faint ghost slot (typeSlugs ghost) always waiting at the end of the line for the next sort. The drops are synced to the narration: one slug lands on each of 'back', 'word', 'by', 'word'. A tiny caption sits bottom-right in IBM Plex Mono: 'illustration'. No lab, no product, no logo anywhere. The person's profile is just visible as a dark shoulder edge at frame left.

shots.visual: THIS SHOT: the lamp clicks on in the detective's study; the hands pin the case card WHO TAUGHT IT? and file the makers' own admission of a flaw. CAMERA: BOARD (the lamp's pool resolving onto the empty board; the K pin a 1–2 s insert), then FILE (top-down on the desk for the slip and its fold). Lamp change (a real mood change, serverCyan to candleAmber; the line waits for the lamp): the frozen earth's last cyan window becomes the switch-click of a green-shaded banker's lamp (props/lights bankersLamp). A book-lined study builds out of the dark around the lamp's pool: shelves as ink silhouettes against an amber backlight, haze drifting through the lamplight. In the pool, a dark corkboard (the Case Board) on the wall above a writing desk, empty but for faint pin-holes marking its slots. BOARD MAP (canonical, from the staging appendix; repeated word for word): the Case Board is a fixed grid of slots laid out as network columns by era, left to right: C1 (1943–1969) the far-left input column, C2 (1969–1997), C3 (2006–2017), C4 (2018–2023), and the output, the glowing chat box, at the far right; the case card WHO TAUGHT IT? hangs in slot K at the board's centre; the suspect cards S1 RULES, S2 KNOWLEDGE and S3 LEARNING hang in the left margin, top to bottom; the founding row F1–F2 runs beneath columns C3 and C4; the question-card thread runs along the board's top edge (slots Q1 to Q4, left to right), a low-chroma oxblood string (emberRed rim mixed about 60% into candleAmber) that glints only where the lamp's pool falls; the Wall of Forecasts hangs to the board's right, its slots W1 to W8 left to right (W1 Turing, W2 chess, W3 Rosenblatt 1961, W4 Florence 2012, W5 Coulom, W6 the 30-to-50-years slip in shadow, W7 Hinton 2017, W8 an empty pin until ch15). The detective is only two steady, cuffed hands (mid-life, not elderly) entering from below frame, never a body, never a face. On 'Who taught it?' the hands pin a single index card in slot K, the centre of the board, with a brass pin: 'WHO TAUGHT IT?' in Special Elite typewriter type. On L0107 the right hand slides a printed strip across the desk into the lamplight and the camera tilts down to it: the launch post's sentence, set as a typed slip with its date (the full launch-post attribution moves to creditsSources), which the narrator reads aloud on L0108 (the text on screen is exactly what is spoken). On 'file' the hands fold the slip once and drop it into a manila folder, close the flap, and tap it twice. The folder stays on the desk at frame right for the rest of the film's study scenes.

shots.visual: THIS SHOT: the three suspect cards RULES, KNOWLEDGE and LEARNING are pinned, then the camera shows the study's whole apparatus: board, candle shelf and Wall of Forecasts. CAMERA: THE FULL WIDE (the first of the three reserved wides), reached in one continuous move: BOARD for the three suspect pins, a tilt down to SHELF for the ghost candles (about 1.8 s), a rise to WALL (about 0.8 s on W6), then an ease back to the full wide itself, board, shelf and Wall in ONE frame with W6's corner half-lit, held for the shot's last 1.5 s. Camera at the board. BOARD MAP (canonical, from the staging appendix; repeated word for word): the Case Board is a fixed grid of slots laid out as network columns by era, left to right: C1 (1943–1969) the far-left input column, C2 (1969–1997), C3 (2006–2017), C4 (2018–2023), and the output, the glowing chat box, at the far right; the case card WHO TAUGHT IT? hangs in slot K at the board's centre; the suspect cards S1 RULES, S2 KNOWLEDGE and S3 LEARNING hang in the left margin, top to bottom; the founding row F1–F2 runs beneath columns C3 and C4; the question-card thread runs along the board's top edge (slots Q1 to Q4, left to right), a low-chroma oxblood string (emberRed rim mixed about 60% into candleAmber) that glints only where the lamp's pool falls; the Wall of Forecasts hangs to the board's right, its slots W1 to W8 left to right (W1 Turing, W2 chess, W3 Rosenblatt 1961, W4 Florence 2012, W5 Coulom, W6 the 30-to-50-years slip in shadow, W7 Hinton 2017, W8 an empty pin until ch15). The hands pin the three suspect cards into the left margin, top to bottom, one per word: 'RULES' in S1 (a paper-cut key over a branching tree), 'KNOWLEDGE' in S2 (a small drawer of index cards), 'LEARNING' in S3 (an unlit paper lantern, paperLantern act 0). Each card is a paper-cut object with its name in Special Elite. Then a slow tilt down past the desk to the long paper-cut shelf beneath the board: the candle-clock, glimpsed for the first time; wordless, in the pause after L0110 (the narration states the candle rule aloud in ch02-s04; here the ghosts only show it). CANDLE-CLOCK RULE (canonical; repeated word for word in every candle shot): every belief candle is cut to the same lit height, 45 scored rings at a pitch of 6 px per ring at L3 (270 px), its flame on the top ring and a small tag at its base giving the year it was lit. It burns down one ring per year the belief is held. The wax that burns away is never lost: it stays above the stub as a ghost paper sleeve, ring-scored and translucent in the haze, so sleeve plus stub is always the full lit height and the SLEEVE's length is the years (16 rings = 96 px; 39 rings = 234 px). The sleeves are the bars of the chart: a longer sleeve means a belief held longer. A candle still lit has a live flame where sleeve meets stub; one put out keeps its sleeve, dark, with a thread of smoke; one that guttered has a frayed rim. Here the shelf is a GLIMPSE OF WHAT THE CASE WILL BUILD: the candles are drawn as pale ghosts (translucent paper outlines in the haze, sleeves and stubs of very different proportions, threads of smoke above several), with a few small flames still burning toward the far right end and one blackened match lying flat; as the camera leaves, the ghosts fade and the shelf stands empty, ready for ch02-s04's first candle at the far left. The camera drifts right along the shelf, then, still wordless (the Wall explains itself; no line names it), rises to the Wall of Forecasts beside the board, lingers on W6, then eases back until board, shelf and Wall share one frame, and holds that full wide through the shot end. Its slots W1 to W5 and W7 hold ghost slips too, pale and unreadable, a few curled at the edges, one pin glinting; they fade as the shelf did. Only W6 is solid and real: one older slip in deep shadow beyond the lamp's reach, only its lower corner catching the lamp, half-lit, its words unreadable (the 30-to-50-years slip, planted here; it has hung there since the board was built and is read in ch13-s01). Nothing is labelled. The lantern on the LEARNING card stays dark.

shots.visual: THIS SHOT: the Rewind: the study runs backwards through five images, a Go stone to a lantern wick, and lands on one lamp in 1940s Chicago. The study image shudders like a stretched tape (horizontal tear lines, a brief warble in the backlight) and begins to run backwards. Five held paper-cut images on an even, unhurried cadence, one per beat (goStone, fans, snow, knob, wick), at exactly the same spacing as the final chapter's fast-forward so the two read as one rhyme. Each runs in reverse motion, in strict reverse order of time, so that the final chapter's fast-forward can replay them forwards; the last ember dies just before the line enters: (1) a single Go stone lifts off a lit board and floats back up into a silhouette hand (goBoard, perspective); (2) inside a dark desktop tower, two graphics-card fans spin down to stillness and a small status light goes out (desktopTower, gpus 2); (3) snow rises from a white field back into a winter sky, flakes climbing; (4) a large motorised knob on a rack of knobs unturns, its pointer creeping back (perceptronPotRack, a single knob in close-up); (5) a paper lantern's wick goes dark, its glow shrinking to an ember and then nothing (paperLantern act 1 to 0). Nothing is captioned and nothing is explained. On the last ember the tape-shudder stops, the duskRose sky deepens to night, and a date stamp types itself bottom left in Special Elite: 'CHICAGO · 1940s' (decade only, so ch02's c. 1941 and 1943 stamps both sit inside it). Narration begins only after the fifth image. On 'Chicago' a single lamp clicks on in a distant window of a 1940s brick building silhouetted against the night.

shots.visual: THIS SHOT: the title, cut from black card, is backlit over the Chicago night, and a small lantern's wick catches. The distant Chicago window's lamplight swells until it fills the frame with a warm amber backlight and haze. Across it, a sheet of black card slides in on L1, and the title is cut out of it so the light pours through the letters: WHO TAUGHT THE MACHINE? Each letter's cut edge carries a hairline rim; motes drift through the letterforms. A beat later the subtitle fades up beneath in Cormorant italic, ink on light: 'A case history of neural networks, 1943–2026'. Below the title, very small, a single paper lantern hangs unlit on a thread. On the closing beat (wickCatch) its wick catches with the third note of the motif withheld: a pinpoint of flame, nothing more. Hold, then a slow fade to the warm dark.
